label: <DEL> step when the sequence starts with i/l/h
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, i.e. while emitting original token 0) and never in the original or copy phases. Within delimiter steps it is very sparse (about 0.4%) and is gated by the first original token, which is also the token being output: i, l and h make up about 83% of activation mass, with a small tail on 3 and 2. Magnitude is larger and firing more likely when the last original token (the input just before <DEL>) is v (48% of mass), and to a lesser degree j, 1 or t; L = 3 is overrepresented. Even with all of these conditions most matching delimiter steps stay inactive (precision is at most ~0.3), so the exact trigger depends on hidden state this description does not capture. Does not fire on any non-delimiter step.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=v (+4.50), phase=1 & out_tok=l (+4.33), phase=1 & out_tok=i (+4.05), phase=1 & out_tok=h (+3.15), prev_tok=j (+2.49), prev_tok=t (+1.88). Lower it: in_first=0 (-3.12), in_count=1 (-2.08), orig2=q (-1.88), prev_tok=0 (-1.59).
